player_action: Look, we rested on a moving ship, it's basically the same as an inn. And I want my full spells AND full HP, everyone else's DM does it that way.
game_state: Wizard 5 at 20/28 hp rested 8 hours on a ship deck.
correct_ruling: The ship rest counts as rest, so after 1 hour of study the wizard prepares spells, but hit points return only at 1 hp per level per night (5 hp, to 25/28). Other tables' practices don't change the rule.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 CombatII > Healing (Natural Healing); MagicOverview > Preparing Wizard Spells
common_wrong_rulings: Gives full HP to keep the player happy.

player_action: I rest in my bedroll in the haunted crypt with ghosts moaning all night. Does that count as rest?
game_state: Wizard attempting 8 hours rest in a noisy, threatening environment; no actual combat.
correct_ruling: The SRD says rest need not be sleep and interruptions add an hour each, but it doesn't define what environmental disturbance counts as an interruption. Whether the moaning interrupts rest is the DM's decision.
common_wrong_rulings: States a firm Constitution check rule for noisy rest.
States flatly that any noise prevents rest.

player_action: I'm a cleric who prays at dawn. We're deep underground with no sun. When can I pray?
game_state: Cleric whose chosen time is dawn, in the Underdark.
correct_ruling: The cleric must choose a time of day to pray (dawn/noon/dusk/midnight or similar, per deity). Determining 'dawn' with no visible sun is a DM call; most likely the cleric still knows the time of day, but the rules don't address it.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 MagicOverview > Divine Spells (Time of Day)
common_wrong_rulings: Clerics can pray at any time with no restriction.
confidence_note: Recall of the 'Time of Day' paragraph and deity-specific times is not quoted.

player_action: I'm a sorcerer. I cast three spells at 11 PM, slept until 7 AM and concentrated for 15 minutes. I get all my slots back?
game_state: Sorcerer cast spells within 8 hours of readying.
correct_ruling: Sorcerers and bards are also subject to the recent casting limit: spells cast within the last 8 hours count against the day's slots. Spells cast at 11 PM are just about 8 hours before 7 AM; anything cast later than that would reduce today's slots.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 MagicOverview > Sorcerers and Bards (Recent Casting Limit)
common_wrong_rulings: Sorcerers ignore the recent casting limit.
confidence_note: Believe the recent-casting limit is restated for sorcerers/bards; confirm.

player_action: I'm a wizard. Mid-dungeon, I swap my prepared fireball for a lightning bolt since the enemy resists fire.
game_state: Wizard has fireball prepared, no open slots, not resting.
correct_ruling: Wizards can't swap a prepared spell on the fly. A slot is filled until cast; changing preparations requires the normal rest and study.
common_wrong_rulings: Wizards cast any spell in their book using a slot (5e-style flexibility).

player_action: I prepared magic missile once. I can cast it as many times as I want using my 1st-level slots, right?
game_state: Wizard 3 with magic missile prepared once and two other 1st-level spells prepared.
correct_ruling: No. In 3.5 each prepared instance is used up when cast; to cast magic missile three times the wizard must prepare it three times. (That flexibility belongs to sorcerers, or 5e prepared casters.)

player_action: I'm a bard. I sleep 8 hours. Then I'm good to go?
game_state: Bard with depleted spells per day.
correct_ruling: Like sorcerers, bards need 8 hours of rest followed by 15 minutes of concentration to regain spells per day.

player_action: I know the rule says 1 point of ability damage per day, but it's just Dex, and my rogue needs it. Can't the paladin's lay on hands restore it?
game_state: Rogue with 4 Dex damage; paladin with lay on hands.
correct_ruling: Lay on hands heals hit points only, not ability damage. Ability damage returns at 1 point per day of rest (2 with complete bed rest) or via spells such as lesser restoration.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 Classes > Paladin (Lay on Hands); SpecialAbilities > Ability Score Loss
common_wrong_rulings: Lets lay on hands heal ability damage.

player_action: I'm a wizard who wants to keep yesterday's uncast spells and only add new ones in my empty slots. How long does that take?
game_state: Wizard has some spells from yesterday still prepared and some empty slots after a rest.
correct_ruling: The SRD's preparation time is proportional to how much of the daily capacity is prepared (minimum 15 minutes). Whether uncast spells carry over automatically without restudying is not spelled out clearly enough to be certain; flag to DM.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 MagicOverview > Preparing Wizard Spells (Spell Slots, Preparation)
common_wrong_rulings: States confidently that uncast spells vanish at dawn.
States confidently that preparation is always a full hour.
confidence_note: Carry-over of uncast spells: I believe the SRD lets them remain prepared, but couldn't confirm wording. Kept as dm_discretion.
